title: Motion and Kinematics
seo_title: Kinematics Worksheets: Velocity, Acceleration and Free Fall (High School Physics)
standard_text: Analyze data to support the claim that Newton's second law of motion describes the mathematical relationship among the net force on a macroscopic object, its mass, and its acceleration.
meta_desc: Free high school physics worksheets on motion and kinematics (NGSS HS-PS2-1): speed and velocity, acceleration, motion equations, free fall and motion graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Use v = u + at and d = ut + ½at² for constant acceleration.
body_html:
How to think about it

Kinematics describes how position and velocity change with time.

  • v = d ÷ t (steady speed). a = (v − u) ÷ t.
  • With constant acceleration: v = u + at and d = ut + ½at². Free fall: a = g = 9.8 m/s².
  • Slope of position-time = velocity; slope of velocity-time = acceleration.
Example

0 to 20 m/s in 4 s. Acceleration?

(20 − 0) ÷ 4

Answer: 5 m/s²

Example

Dropped for 2 s. Distance?

4.9 × 2²

Answer: 19.6 m

Common mistakes

  • Treating speed and velocity as the same.
  • Thinking a steady speed on a curve means no acceleration.
  • Using d = vt when the object is accelerating.

faq.q: What is the difference between speed and velocity?
faq.a: Speed tells how fast; velocity tells how fast and in which direction.
Subtract the starting velocity from the final velocity and divide by the time: a = (v − u) ÷ t.

faq.q: What is the acceleration due to gravity?
faq.a: Near Earth's surface, falling objects accelerate at about 9.8 m/s² when air resistance is small.

items.q: A car goes around a curve at a steady 20 m/s. Is it accelerating?
c: Yes, because its direction is changing.
